Meridian Analytics Inc. — Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2024
Financial Highlights
Meridian Analytics Inc. reported total revenue of $84.2 million for fiscal
year 2024, representing a 19% increase over the prior year. Net income was
$11.6 million, up from $8.9 million in FY2023, driven primarily by growth in
the company's enterprise data analytics segment.
Segment Performance
The Enterprise Analytics segment contributed $52.3 million in revenue, while
the Consulting Services segment contributed $31.9 million. Enterprise
Analytics grew 27% year-over-year, outpacing Consulting Services growth of
8%.
Operating Expenses
Total operating expenses were $68.1 million, including $22.4 million in
research and development, $18.7 million in sales and marketing, and $14.3
million in general and administrative costs.
Headcount
The company ended FY2024 with 612 full-time employees, an increase of 84 from
the prior year, with the largest growth in the Engineering and Data Science
departments.
Outlook
Management expects FY2025 revenue growth in the range of 15% to 20%, driven
by continued expansion of the Enterprise Analytics product line and planned
entry into the European market in the second half of the fiscal year.

Meridian Analytics Inc. — Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2025
Financial Highlights
Meridian Analytics Inc. reported total revenue of $101.7 million for fiscal year 
2025, a 20.8% increase over FY2024's $84.2 million. Net income rose to $15.2 
million, compared to $11.6 million in the prior year.
Segment Performance
Enterprise Analytics revenue reached $68.9 million, growing 31.7% year-over-year 
and now representing 68% of total company revenue. Consulting Services grew more 
modestly to $32.8 million.
European Expansion
As previously guided, the company launched operations in the United Kingdom and 
Germany in Q3 FY2025, contributing $4.1 million in revenue in its first two 
quarters and establishing a 22-person regional team based in London.
Operating Expenses
Total operating expenses were $82.6 million, including $28.1 million in research 
and development, reflecting continued investment in the company's retrieval and 
evaluation tooling for AI-driven analytics products.
Headcount
The company ended FY2025 with 731 full-time employees, an increase of 119 from 
FY2024.
Outlook
Management expects FY2026 revenue growth of 18% to 22%, with European operations 
expected to reach profitability by Q4 FY2026.

Expense Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Purpose
This policy governs how employees incur and report business expenses on behalf 
of Meridian Analytics Inc. All expenses must be reasonable, necessary for 
business purposes, and properly documented.
Approval Limits
Expenses under $100 may be self-approved by the employee and submitted for 
reimbursement. Expenses between $100 and $1,000 require manager approval. 
Expenses above $1,000 require both manager and Finance Director approval before 
being incurred.
Receipts
Original itemized receipts are required for any expense over $25. Credit card 
statements alone are not sufficient documentation. Receipts must be uploaded to 
the expense system within 14 days of the transaction.
Non-Reimbursable Items
The company will not reimburse personal entertainment, traffic or parking fines, 
spa or gym charges, or alcohol purchased without a client present. Any 
exceptions must be approved in writing by the Finance Director.
Corporate Cards
Employees who travel frequently may be issued a corporate card. Corporate card 
transactions must still be logged in the expense system with a business 
justification, even though no reimbursement is required.

Reimbursement Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Submission Window
All reimbursement requests must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. 
Requests submitted after 60 days will not be reimbursed except under documented 
extenuating circumstances approved by the Finance Director.
Payment Timeline
Approved reimbursements are paid out within the next two payroll cycles 
following approval, via direct deposit to the employee's registered bank 
account.
Currency and Exchange Rates
Expenses incurred in a foreign currency are converted to USD using the exchange 
rate on the date of the transaction, as reflected on the employee's card 
statement. Manually calculated conversions are not accepted.
Disputed Reimbursements
If an employee disputes a rejected reimbursement, they may appeal in writing to 
the Finance Director within 10 business days of the rejection, including any 
additional supporting documentation.
Advances
Employees traveling internationally for more than 5 days may request a cash 
advance of up to $500 through Finance, which is reconciled against actual 
expenses upon their return.

Travel Expense Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Booking Travel
All flights and hotels must be booked through the company's designated travel 
portal to ensure duty-of-care tracking and negotiated corporate rates. 
Exceptions require Finance Director approval in advance.
Flight Class
Domestic flights under 5 hours must be booked in economy class. International 
flights over 8 hours may be booked in premium economy or business class with 
Director-level approval.
Hotel Limits
Standard hotel spend is capped at $250 per night in major metro areas (e.g., New 
York, San Francisco, London) and $180 per night elsewhere, unless a conference 
rate requires a different property.
Meals While Traveling
Employees may claim up to $75 per day for meals while traveling on approved 
business trips, itemized as breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Alcohol is only 
reimbursable when entertaining a client, up to $50 per event.
Ground Transportation
Ride-share and taxi expenses are reimbursable for airport transfers and client 
meetings. Personal vehicle use is reimbursed at the current IRS standard mileage 
rate, calculated from the employee's regular office location.
Combining Personal Travel
Employees may extend a business trip for personal travel, but the company will 
only cover the cost equivalent to the business-only itinerary; any price 
difference is the employee's responsibility.

Employee Handbook — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Section 1: Purpose and Scope
This handbook applies to all full-time, part-time, and contract employees of 
Meridian Analytics Inc. It summarizes company policies, employee expectations, 
and available benefits. It does not constitute an employment contract.
Section 2: Working Hours
Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, with a 
one-hour unpaid lunch break. Employees in engineering and data roles may use 
flexible scheduling with manager approval, provided they are available during 
core hours of 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
Section 3: Code of Conduct
Employees are expected to act with integrity, treat colleagues with respect, and 
avoid conflicts of interest. Harassment of any kind, including based on race, 
gender, religion, disability, or sexual orientation, will result in disciplinary 
action up to and including termination.
Section 4: Performance Reviews
Formal performance reviews occur twice a year, in June and December. Reviews are 
conducted by the employee's direct manager and include a self-assessment, 
manager assessment, and goal-setting for the next cycle. Compensation 
adjustments are typically communicated within four weeks of the December review.
Section 5: Confidentiality
All employees must sign a confidentiality agreement at the time of hiring. 
Proprietary information, client data, and internal financial figures may not be 
disclosed to any third party without written authorization from the Legal 
department.
Section 6: Grievance Procedure
Employees who wish to raise a concern about a colleague, manager, or workplace 
condition should first speak with their manager. If the issue is not resolved, 
or involves the manager directly, the employee may escalate to HR via the 
confidential HR portal.

Parental Leave Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
1. Eligibility
All employees who have completed at least six months of continuous employment 
are eligible for parental leave, regardless of gender or the manner in which 
they became a parent (birth, adoption, or surrogacy).
2. Duration
Primary caregivers are entitled to 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Secondary 
caregivers are entitled to 6 weeks of paid leave. Leave must be taken within 12 
months of the birth or placement of the child, and may be split into two blocks 
with manager approval.
3. Pay During Leave
Parental leave is paid at 100% of base salary for the eligible duration. This 
does not include bonus or commission components, which are prorated based on 
actual days worked in the relevant period.
4. Application Process
Employees must notify their manager and HR at least 30 days before the expected 
start of leave, where practicable. A parental leave request form must be 
submitted through the HR portal along with supporting documentation (e.g., due 
date letter, adoption confirmation).
5. Job Protection
Employees returning from parental leave are guaranteed reinstatement to the same 
or an equivalent role, with the same pay, benefits, and seniority, provided the 
leave did not exceed the policy maximum.
6. Exceptions
Employees on active performance improvement plans (PIPs) at the time of their 
leave request will have their PIP paused during leave and resumed upon return, 
rather than being extended or cancelled.

Remote Work Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Eligibility
Employees in roles that do not require regular on-site presence (e.g., most 
Engineering, Data, and certain Finance roles) may work remotely up to 3 days per 
week, subject to manager approval. Fully remote arrangements require Director-
level sign-off.
Equipment
The company provides a laptop, monitor, and a one-time $400 home office stipend 
for employees approved for regular remote work. Additional equipment requests 
are reviewed by IT on a case-by-case basis.
Core Collaboration Hours
Remote employees must be available and responsive during core hours of 11:00 AM 
to 4:00 PM in their local time zone, aligned with the standard working hours 
defined in the Employee Handbook.
Security Requirements
Remote employees must connect to company systems via the corporate VPN and must 
not access client data from personal, unencrypted devices, in line with the IT 
Security Policy.
International Remote Work
Employees wishing to work remotely from a country other than their country of 
employment must obtain approval from HR and Legal at least 6 weeks in advance, 
due to tax and employment law considerations.

Sick Leave Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Entitlement
All employees receive 10 paid sick days per calendar year, credited in full at 
the start of employment or on January 1st for existing employees. Sick leave 
does not carry over to the following year.
Notification
Employees should notify their manager as early as possible on the day of 
absence, ideally before the start of their normal working hours. For absences 
longer than three consecutive days, a note from a healthcare provider may be 
requested by HR.
Extended Illness
Employees requiring more than 10 sick days in a year due to a serious health 
condition may apply for extended medical leave, which may be unpaid or covered 
by short-term disability insurance depending on tenure and plan enrollment.
Sick Leave for Family Care
Employees may use up to 5 of their 10 annual sick days to care for an immediate 
family member (spouse, child, or parent) who is ill.
Misuse
Repeated or suspected misuse of sick leave will be addressed through the 
standard HR grievance and disciplinary process, in coordination with the 
employee's manager.

Vacation Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Accrual
Full-time employees accrue 1.75 days of paid vacation per month, totaling 21 
days per year. Accrual begins on the first day of employment, but new hires may 
not use accrued vacation during their first 90 days.
Carryover
Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused vacation days into the following 
calendar year. Any days beyond this cap are forfeited on December 31st unless 
local law requires otherwise.
Requesting Time Off
Vacation requests should be submitted at least two weeks in advance through the 
HR portal for approval by the employee's manager. Requests during the last two 
weeks of December require additional lead time due to company-wide blackout 
scheduling.
Unused Vacation at Termination
Upon voluntary or involuntary termination, employees are paid out for unused 
accrued vacation days at their current base salary rate, in accordance with 
state and local law.
Part-Time Employees
Part-time employees accrue vacation on a prorated basis according to their 
contracted hours per week, calculated using the same 1.75-day-per-month formula 
applied to full-time equivalent hours.

Acceptable Use Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Scope
This policy governs the acceptable use of company-owned devices, networks,
and accounts, including email, cloud storage, and internal collaboration
tools, by all employees and contractors.
Permitted Use
Company systems are provided primarily for business purposes. Limited
personal use is permitted, provided it does not interfere with work
responsibilities, consume excessive resources, or violate any other company
policy.
Prohibited Activities
Employees may not use company systems to access illegal content, install
unauthorized software, circumvent security controls, or run personal side
businesses. Installing browser extensions or applications not approved by IT
is prohibited on managed devices.
Email and Communication
Company email should not be used to send Restricted or Confidential data to
personal email accounts. Auto-forwarding rules that send company email to
external addresses are disabled by default and require IT Security approval
to enable.
Monitoring
The company reserves the right to monitor use of company systems, including
email and internet activity, for security, compliance, and legal purposes,
consistent with applicable law and the IT Security Policy.
Enforcement
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and
including termination, and in some cases may be referred to Legal or law
enforcement, particularly where illegal activity is involved.

Access Control Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Principle of Least Privilege
Employees are granted the minimum level of system access required to perform
their job duties. Additional access must be requested through the IT access
request system and approved by both the requester's manager and the relevant
system owner.
Role-Based Access
Access to systems is assigned based on standardized role templates (e.g.,
"Data Analyst," "Finance Associate") wherever possible, rather than ad-hoc
individual permissions, to simplify auditing and reduce configuration drift.
Access Reviews
System owners must review user access lists for Confidential and Restricted
systems on a quarterly basis and revoke any access that is no longer
necessary, including for employees who have changed roles internally.
Privileged Access
Administrative or privileged access to production systems requires additional
approval from IT Security and is logged separately for audit purposes.
Privileged accounts must not be used for routine, non-administrative tasks.
Offboarding
All system access must be revoked within 4 hours of an employee's termination
being processed by HR, in line with the Employment Termination Policy,
regardless of whether the termination is voluntary or involuntary.

Incident Response Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Severity Levels
Incidents are classified as Severity 1 (critical, client-impacting or data
breach), Severity 2 (significant but contained), or Severity 3 (minor, no
immediate business impact). Severity 1 incidents trigger immediate escalation
to the CTO and Legal.
Response Timeline
Severity 1 incidents must be acknowledged by the on-call IT Security engineer
within 15 minutes and must have an initial containment action within 1 hour.
Severity 2 incidents must be acknowledged within 2 hours.
Communication Protocol
For any incident involving potential client data exposure, the Legal
department and affected client's designated contact must be notified within
24 hours of confirmation, in accordance with contractual and regulatory
obligations.
Post-Incident Review
Within 5 business days of resolving a Severity 1 or Severity 2 incident, the
IT Security team must produce a post-incident report covering root cause,
timeline, impact, and remediation steps, to be reviewed by leadership.
Data Breach Notification
In the event of a confirmed data breach involving personal data, Legal will
determine notification obligations under applicable law (e.g., GDPR, state
breach notification laws) and coordinate the notification process with
affected individuals and regulators as required.

Password Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Minimum Requirements
Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and include a mix of uppercase
letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Passwords may
not reuse any of the employee's last 10 passwords.
Multi-Factor Authentication
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all systems classified as
handling Confidential or Restricted data, including email, the HR portal, and
the client data warehouse. SMS-based MFA is discouraged in favor of
authenticator apps or hardware keys.
Password Expiration
Passwords for standard corporate accounts expire every 180 days. Passwords
for administrative or privileged accounts expire every 90 days and require
approval from IT Security to reset outside the normal cycle.
Password Managers
Employees are required to use the company-approved password manager for
storing credentials to work systems. Storing passwords in browsers,
spreadsheets, or plain text files is prohibited under this policy.
Account Lockout
Accounts are automatically locked after 5 consecutive failed login attempts
within a 15-minute window. Locked accounts can be unlocked by the employee
via self-service identity verification or by contacting the IT Helpdesk.

IT Security Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Purpose
This policy establishes baseline security requirements for all systems,
applications, and data handled by Meridian Analytics Inc., in order to
protect company and client information from unauthorized access, disclosure,
or loss.
Data Classification
All data must be classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted.
Client data and financial records are classified as Restricted by default and
require the highest level of access control and encryption.
Encryption Requirements
Restricted and Confidential data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and
in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Unencrypted storage of Restricted data on
laptops or removable media is strictly prohibited.
Incident Reporting
Any suspected security incident, including lost devices, phishing attempts,
or unauthorized access, must be reported to the IT Security team within 1
hour of discovery via the security hotline or incident portal.
Security Training
All employees must complete annual security awareness training. New hires
must complete this training within their first 2 weeks of employment, before
being granted access to Confidential or Restricted systems.
Third-Party Access
External vendors and contractors requiring system access must be provisioned
with time-limited accounts, reviewed quarterly, and immediately revoked upon
contract completion or termination, in coordination with the Vendor Agreement
Policy.

Master Services Agreement — Client: Brightfield Retail Group
This Master Services Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between Meridian
Analytics Inc. ("Provider") and Brightfield Retail Group ("Client") for the
provision of data analytics consulting services.
Scope of Services
Provider will deliver quarterly customer segmentation analysis, inventory
demand forecasting models, and a monthly executive dashboard, as further
detailed in each Statement of Work (SOW) executed under this Agreement.
Term
This Agreement has an initial term of 24 months from the Effective Date, and
will automatically renew for successive 12-month periods unless either party
provides 90 days' written notice of non-renewal.
Fees
Client agrees to pay Provider a monthly retainer of $45,000, plus any
additional project fees specified in individual SOWs. Invoices are due within
30 days of receipt.
Data Ownership and Confidentiality
All Client data provided to Provider remains the exclusive property of
Client. Provider may not use Client data for any purpose outside the scope of
this Agreement, including training of general-purpose machine learning
models, without Client's prior written consent.
Termination for Cause
Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon material breach by
the other party that remains uncured 30 days after written notice.
Limitation of Liability
Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees
paid by Client in the 12 months preceding the claim, except in cases of gross
negligence or willful misconduct.

Master Services Agreement — Client: Halden Manufacturing Corp
This Master Services Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between Meridian
Analytics Inc. ("Provider") and Halden Manufacturing Corp ("Client") for
predictive maintenance analytics services.
Scope of Services
Provider will deploy and maintain a predictive maintenance model for Client's
manufacturing equipment, deliver weekly anomaly reports, and provide on-call
support for critical alerts during Client's production hours.
Term
This Agreement has an initial term of 36 months from the Effective Date.
Early termination by Client prior to month 18 requires payment of an early
termination fee equal to 3 months of retainer fees.
Fees
Client agrees to pay Provider a monthly retainer of $62,000. Fees are subject
to an annual increase of up to 4%, tied to the Consumer Price Index,
beginning in the second year of the Agreement.
Service Level Agreement
Provider guarantees 99.5% uptime for the predictive maintenance dashboard and
a response time of under 2 hours for critical anomaly alerts during Client's
production hours. Failure to meet the SLA in two consecutive months entitles
Client to a service credit of 10% of that month's fee.
Data Ownership and Confidentiality
Sensor and equipment data provided by Client remains Client's property.
Provider may retain de-identified, aggregated data for internal model
improvement purposes only, as permitted under Section 8.2.
Limitation of Liability
Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees
paid by Client in the 12 months preceding the claim, except in cases of gross
negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of confidentiality obligations.

Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
When an NDA Is Required
An NDA must be executed before any confidential information is shared with a
prospective client, vendor, contractor, or partner, including during early-
stage sales conversations and technical due diligence.
Standard vs. Mutual NDAs
The Legal department maintains two templates: a one-way NDA (used when only
Meridian's information will be disclosed) and a mutual NDA (used when both
parties will share confidential information). Sales and Business Development
should default to the mutual template unless directed otherwise by Legal.
Approval and Signing Authority
NDAs based on the standard templates may be signed by any Director-level
employee or above. Any deviation from the standard template language must be
reviewed and approved by Legal before signing, regardless of the signer's
seniority.
Term of Confidentiality Obligations
Standard NDAs impose confidentiality obligations for 3 years from the date of
disclosure, or 5 years for NDAs involving trade secrets or proprietary
machine learning methodologies.
Record Keeping
All executed NDAs must be uploaded to the central contract repository within
5 business days of signing, tagged with the counterparty name and expiration
date, so Legal can track upcoming renewals or expirations.

Employment Termination Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Voluntary Resignation
Employees are asked to provide at least two weeks' written notice of
resignation. Employees in Director-level roles or above are encouraged to
provide four weeks' notice to support a smooth transition.
Involuntary Termination
Involuntary terminations must be reviewed and approved by HR and, for cause-
based terminations, by Legal, prior to being communicated to the employee.
This ensures consistent application of policy and reduces legal risk.
Final Pay
Final paychecks, including payout of unused accrued vacation as described in
the Vacation Policy, are issued no later than the next regular payroll cycle
following the termination date, or sooner where required by state law.
Severance
Employees terminated as part of a reduction-in-force (RIF) are eligible for
severance pay of two weeks' base salary per year of service, with a minimum
of four weeks, contingent on signing a standard separation agreement.
Return of Company Property
All company property, including laptops, access badges, and any physical
documents, must be returned on or before the employee's last day. Failure to
do so may result in the cost being deducted from final pay where permitted by
law.
Exit Interviews
HR conducts an exit interview with all departing employees to gather feedback
on their experience and identify any outstanding concerns before their
departure.

Vendor Agreement Policy — Meridian Analytics Inc.
Vendor Onboarding
All new vendors must complete a security and compliance questionnaire
administered by the IT Security team before any contract is signed,
particularly for vendors who will process client or employee data.
Standard Payment Terms
Unless otherwise negotiated, vendor agreements use Net 45 payment terms.
Vendors requesting Net 30 or faster payment terms must be approved by the
Finance Director, as this may affect cash flow planning.
Data Processing Vendors
Vendors that process personal data on Meridian's behalf (e.g., cloud
infrastructure, analytics tools) must sign a Data Processing Addendum (DPA)
in addition to the main vendor agreement, and must demonstrate SOC 2 Type II
compliance or equivalent.
Termination Rights
Standard vendor agreements include a termination-for-convenience clause
allowing Meridian to exit the agreement with 60 days' written notice, except
for vendors providing critical infrastructure, which require 120 days'
notice.
Renewal Review
Vendor agreements above $50,000 in annual spend are reviewed by Procurement
and Finance 90 days before renewal to evaluate performance, pricing, and
whether the vendor relationship should continue.
